title: What If a Particle Beam Went Through Your Head? In 1978 One Did

scenes.text: What if a particle beam went straight through your head? In 1978, it happened to a physicist.
He leaned into the Soviet Union's largest accelerator to check a faulty part, just as the safety systems failed.
Protons near light speed went in the back of his head and out beside his nose. No pain.
He saw a flash brighter than a thousand suns. The dose was about two thousand gray. Five is usually fatal.
Within days his face swelled and skin peeled along the beam's path. Doctors expected him to die.
He didn't. He lost hearing in one ear, and half his face froze. Then he finished his doctorate and went back to physics.

description:
What if a particle accelerator beam went through your head? In 1978 the Soviet physicist Anatoli Bugorski leaned into the U-70 synchrotron at Protvino, then the largest accelerator in the Soviet Union, and a 76 GeV proton beam passed through the back of his head and out beside his nose.
He reported a flash brighter than a thousand suns and no pain. The dose is put at about 2,000 gray going in and 3,000 coming out; more than 5 gray is usually fatal. He lost the hearing in his left ear and the left side of his face was paralysed, but he completed his PhD and kept working as a physicist.
